newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SAVINGS BANK DEPOSITS HIT ONE BILLION LITAS.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS BANK DEPOSITS HIT ONE BILLION LITAS.

text.p: Deposits in the state-owned Lithuanian Savings Bank have hit one billion litas for the first time, the bank said on Wednesday.
"This year on June 17, individual deposits in Lithuanian Savings Bank hit one billion litas," the bank said a statement.
"In no Lithuanian state commercial bank, either between the wars or in the newly independent Lithuania, has such an amount been seen before," the bank added.
"Currently 57 percent of individual deposits held in commercial banks are held in Savings Bank," the statement said.
That figure was up from 52 percent at the beginning of the year. The bank said that individual deposits had grown consistently over the past four years.
Deposits hit 291 million litas in 1993, 462 million litas in 1994, 772 million litas in 1995 and 888 million litas in 1996.

The government has announced plans to privatise the Lithuanian State Commercial Bank and the Bank of Agriculture but officials say they are holding off on Savings Bank to see how the first two privatisations go.
